OpenZeppelin TimelockController execution: the target and value are the ones fixed when the operation was scheduled by a proposer and waited its delay in public (REQ-ACCESS-021, SPEC-GOV-002); forwarding them is the timelock's purpose. Anyone may trigger execution, but nobody can change the target or value. Covered by TEST-194, TEST-212, PROP-058.
Same as execute: targets and values are fixed at scheduling and waited their delay; executeBatch forwards them unchanged.

Every external call of deposit and claim runs under the escrow's transient reentrancy flag, which is the first check of both functions (REQ-ESCROW-007): a callback into deposit or claim reverts Reentrancy before reading or writing any state, and the escrow has no other state-changing function. The flagged call is ILock.holder(), a view (STATICCALL) of the immutable protocol Lock, which can change no state; the check must precede the credit (REQ-ESCROW-002). Covered by TEST-179 (depositReentryReverts), PROP-037, PROP-052.

Every external call of deposit and claim runs under the escrow's transient reentrancy flag, which is the first check of both functions (REQ-ESCROW-007): a callback into deposit or claim reverts Reentrancy before reading or writing any state, and the escrow has no other state-changing function. The flagged call is the token's balanceOf (a view, STATICCALL); measuring the balance before and after the pull is the specified way to credit what arrived (REQ-ESCROW-003), so the credit is necessarily written after these calls. Covered by TEST-179, PROP-052 (Halmos and Certora).

Same as the balanceOf before the pull: the measured rise is the credit (REQ-ESCROW-003), so the credit cannot be written before it is known. A token callback during safeTransferFrom finds the flag set (TEST-179 depositReentryReverts, PayoutEscrowProperties).

Every external call of deposit and claim runs under the escrow's transient reentrancy flag, which is the first check of both functions (REQ-ESCROW-007): a callback into deposit or claim reverts Reentrancy before reading or writing any state, and the escrow has no other state-changing function. The flagged call is ILock.isLocked(), a view (STATICCALL) of the immutable protocol Lock; the LockHeld check must precede the effects (REQ-ESCROW-004). The token transfer itself comes after every state write (checks-effects-interactions). Covered by TEST-179, PROP-052.

The _lpVaultOf write follows only view calls to the LPVault (INTEGRATION_ID, COLLATERALIZATION, LOCK, AMM_PROTOCOL) and to Collateralization (LOCK), declared view in ILPVault/ICollateralizationViews and therefore compiled to STATICCALL, which cannot change state or re-enter a state-changing function. The function is callable only by the AvanaTimelock after the normal delay (REQ-VTOKEN-044), and every storage check precedes the calls. Covered by TEST-024 (registration rejections) and PROP-055 (Halmos check_PROP_055_registrationIsWriteOnce).

The calls before the `totalCovered` write are the view reads `HUB.getSpokeDeficitRay` and `HUB.getSpokeAddedAssets` (through `fundedBalance()`), compiled as STATICCALL to the immutable Aave V4 Hub, so they cannot re-enter or change state; `totalCovered` needs the amount those reads determine (SPEC-FLR-001), and it is written before the one state-changing call, `HUB.eliminateDeficit` (REQ-FLR-006, REQ-FLR-018). The function is also non-reentrant (transient guard) and `restricted` to COVERAGE_ROLE. Covered by TEST-199, PROP-039, PROP-060.

The call before the allowlist write is the view check `HUB.isSpokeListed(ASSET_ID, spoke)` required by REQ-FLR-017, a STATICCALL to the immutable Aave V4 Hub that cannot re-enter or change state; the function makes no state-changing external call, is non-reentrant (transient guard) and `restricted` to RESERVE_ADMIN_ROLE. Covered by TEST-288 allowlistRules, TEST-199.

Each write forwards to one of the six logic contracts held in implementation immutables, checked at construction through logicConfig() (kind and the hash of every implementation immutable) and changed only by an upgrade at the normal delay; no address comes from calldata or storage, and the caller's role is checked before the delegatecall (REQ-CONFIG-001, REQ-CONFIG-002).

Constructor only. The calls are view functions, compiled to STATICCALL, so the callee cannot change any state; and during construction the route has no runtime code, so a callback into it runs nothing. The state written afterwards is immutables only, which do not exist until the constructor returns. The checks fix the GSM legs against the wrapper and module (REQ-ROUTE-011, REQ-ROUTE-045) and fail closed with InvalidRouteConfig.

Constructor only. decimals() is a view function, compiled to STATICCALL, so the callee cannot change any state; and during construction the route has no runtime code, so a callback into it runs nothing. The state written afterwards is immutables only (_GEM_CONVERSION and the leg addresses). The value fixes the LitePSM conversion factor 10^(18 - decimals) (REQ-ROUTE-012, REQ-ROUTE-045); decimals above 18 revert InvalidRouteConfig.

Constructor only. asset() is a view function, compiled to STATICCALL, so the callee cannot change any state; and during construction the route has no runtime code, so a callback into it runs nothing. The state written afterwards is immutables only. The check fixes the ERC-4626 step against its underlying (REQ-ROUTE-043, REQ-ROUTE-045) and fails closed with InvalidRouteConfig.

The reverts reached from the hop loop are those of SafeCast, forceApprove and the pools themselves: a failed hop must revert the whole swap so that no partial swap or allowance remains, and LPVaultSwap then uses the other route slot (REQ-ROUTE-009, REQ-ROUTE-010). There is no index to find first and no later revert to move it to. The loop runs at most MAX_HOPS = 3 times.

The revert reachable in the residue loop is SafeERC20.safeTransfer of a residue to LPVaultSwap: a residue that cannot be returned must revert the whole swap, because REQ-ROUTE-015 requires every leftover to reach LPVaultSwap in the same call. There is no index to find first. The loop runs over at most five held tokens.

Same finding as Slither unused-return 167f85ddd071f2ec: the hop's output is measured as the route's balance rise, never taken from the returned dy (REQ-ROUTE-009, REQ-ROUTE-015). forge-lint suppression on the line with the reason above it.

Same finding as Slither unused-return e5853431879c99e7: the callback bounds the payment (REQ-ROUTE-013) and the hop's output is measured as the route's balance rise, so the returned deltas are not used.
Same finding as Slither unused-return 5a4d4b1800498ada: the shares minted are measured as the route's static-aToken balance rise (REQ-ROUTE-011, REQ-ROUTE-015).
Same finding as Slither unused-return 5a4d4b1800498ada: the GHO output is LPVaultSwap's measured balance rise and unsold shares are the route's measured residue (REQ-ROUTE-009, REQ-ROUTE-011).

Same finding as Slither unused-return 5a4d4b1800498ada: the USDC output is LPVaultSwap's measured balance rise and DAI below one gem unit is the route's measured residue (REQ-ROUTE-012, REQ-ROUTE-015).
Same finding as Slither unused-return a3356e08d193fad7: the assets are measured as the route's balance rise of the underlying (REQ-ROUTE-008, REQ-ROUTE-015).

ISettlementRoute is named by the `@inheritdoc ISettlementRoute` tags of routeType and dependencies, which must name the interface that declares the function; Aderyn does not count NatSpec references as uses. Removing the import breaks the NatSpec inheritance.
